analysis:
Integrated both supplied analyses against the replayed patches. DistributedInstalledPlan.swift:281–282 propagates the selected prefill schedule; :335–336 and :370 make text-only Gemma serial pipelines default to four lanes, including coordinator-registered pairs. Other visible defaults remain unchanged. This increases concurrent inference exposure relevant to A-001, A-018, TB-007, T-010, T-028 and T-041, but no supplied implementation establishes broken request isolation, unbounded memory admission or failed cancellation. The comments asserting per-request arithmetic/state and live-memory charging are contracts, not verification.
The replayed pair golden changes at expected.json:46–48,67–69,88–90 replace Gemma plan/handoff hashes without changing visible rank splits. Main.swift:66 adds checkGemmaRoutedExperts; its implementation and layout/hash producers are absent. The libs/mlx-swift-lm gitlink at head line 1 changes the inference dependency, but its source delta is not supplied. No visible authorization, attestation, encryption or billing bypass is established.
Material review remains: inspect that dependency delta and lane-owner/session/bridge implementations for request-owned KV/output state, memory charging on every rank, cancellation/retirement fences and width agreement with saved capacity quotes and coordinator admission. Verify arithmetic/model/cache namespace bindings and preservation of T-041 authenticated scope, production SSD gating and staging reservations; existing documented TP cache tiers alone do not demonstrate a new production-cache regression.
Replay is incomplete (8 source units omitted), including the documentation/layout evidence discussed by the local analyses. The revised docs/architecture/inference.md arithmetic and lane-policy sections therefore cannot be independently reconciled here. Review those HEAD sections and qualification restrictions together with the runtime changes before resolving the four-lane default's security implications. These are coverage limits and unverified contracts, not supported vulnerabilities; no concrete regression qualifies for a finding.
